description: Somos un equipo que busca resolver las problemáticas en cuanto a la agricultura local utilizando esos datos para las futuras bases lunares y marcianas. Brindando soluciones, herramientas e información fomentando el interés en la comunidad científica y local.
summary:
To meet the “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data” challenge, we developed a mobile application. Using NASA’s open data, the app allows agricultural producers to assess the conditions of their land and select the seeds best suited to their conditions and goals.
The application enables users to monitor and manage their crops according to their geographic location, while providing relevant data on their plot.
details:
What does it do / How does it work?
The app is organized as a phone-style interface with several views:

Home

  • Shows a weather card with temperature, humidity, wind, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and vapor pressure deficit (VPD).
  • Lets you choose a location, use the browser’s GPS, and sync data.
  • Generates dynamic agronomic advice based on the weather.
  • Quick links to: My Crops, Irrigation Planner, Map, and Tips/Guides.


Agro-Spatial Map

  • Integrates Windy for live wind/weather.
  • Allows to toggle layers: Sentinel-2 NDVI via WMS, water stress/ECOSTRESS, and wind.
  • Includes a NASA POWER panel with a 14-day summary, temperature and precipitation charts, and indicative alerts.

AI Tips and Guides

  • Chat with the Gemini API (optional) and a local backup based on the INTA/CIP catalog.
  • Answers questions about crop rotations, resistant varieties, saline soils, windbreaks, etc.

    3D Irrigation Planner
  • Plot calculator per m² with daily water consumption, full cycle, applied irrigation, and projected harvest.
  • INTA/INASE crops selector: Araucana Potato, Platense Tomato, Quehué Rye, Morrillos Quinoa, Ascasubi Vetch, Salinera Alfalfa.
  • 3D simulator with Three.js of an interactive plot.
  • Soil controls: texture, pH, moisture, temperature, N-P-K, organic matter.
  • Suitability diagnosis, recommendations, and evolution chart.
  • Embedded Windy map for irrigation planning.

    Southern Cross (Beta)
  • Earth–Mars planetary comparator with physical variables: temperature, pressure, humidity, UV radiation, water, gravity.
  • Geographic explorer with Earth analogs, such as the Golfo San Jorge basin and the Atacama.
  • Biophysical simulator on Mars: 1 m² pressurized dome, physical telemetry, control of temperature, volumetric moisture, PPFD, salinity/perchlorates, irrigation, nutrients, and growth of radish, lettuce, or CIP potato.

Benefits

  • Agronomic decision support in contexts of wind, salinity, and water deficit.
  • Water savings through evapotranspiration calculation, water balance, and irrigation planning.
  • Integration of open data: climate, satellites, vegetation indices, and water stress.
  • Use of local/validated varieties: INTA, INASE, and CIP clones.
  • Education and science outreach: Earth–Mars simulator, space crops, and earth analogs.
  • Low barrier to use: mobile interface, in Spanish, with large buttons and guided flows.
  • Resilience: includes a local backup if there is no Gemini API key, and allows manual mode in the simulator.

Expected Impact

  • Producers in southern Patagonia, especially the Golfo San Jorge basin and Comodoro Rivadavia: better irrigation planning and selection of resistant crops.
  • More efficient water use and reduced losses from water stress or salinity.
  • Crop validation for extreme environments, with possible transfer to controlled-environment agriculture.
  • STEM/space education: bringing NASA, remote sensors, and space agriculture closer to students and communities.
  • Foundation for an early warning system and digital agronomic advisory service, if validated with field data.

Tools, Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

Web Languages and Technologies

  • HTML5
  • CSS3 with custom styles
  • Vanilla JavaScript (no evident JS framework)
  • SVG for icons and planets
  • Canvas 2D for evolution charts
  • Tailwind CSS via CDN
  • Google Fonts: Plus Jakarta Sans

Libraries and Services

  • Leaflet 1.9.4 for maps
  • Three.js r128 for 3D simulators
  • Windy Embed for weather maps
  • NASA POWER API for agroclimatic data
  • NASA GIBS WMS for satellite imagery
  • Sentinel Hub WMS (optional) for Sentinel-2 NDVI
  • ECOSTRESS as a water stress reference
  • Gemini API (optional) for the agronomic chat
  • Browser Geolocation API for GPS
  • Images from Unsplash and Wikimedia for backgrounds/illustrations

Hardware

  • Smartphone, tablet, or computer with a modern browser.
  • Device sensors: GPS, if the user grants permission.

Software

  • Web browser.
  • No backend, database, or build process is observed: it is a self-contained front-end prototype.
  • CDNs to load Tailwind, Leaflet, Three.js, and fonts.

How Is the Project Creative?

  • Visual metaphor of a mobile app inside a web page.
  • Dual narrative: real terrestrial agriculture + space exploration.
  • “Southern Cross” as a bridge between Patagonia and Mars, using Earth analogs.
  • Interactive 3D simulators for irrigation and the Martian dome.
  • Gamification: planting, watering, fertilizing, simulating days/sols, and viewing harvest and crop health.
  • Use of real local crops (INTA/CIP) instead of generic crops.
  • Planetary comparator with physical data and a space-themed aesthetic.
  • Dynamic agronomic advice that changes according to climate and soil.

Factors Considered by the Team

  • Local context: salinity, strong winds, water deficit, and Patagonian soils.
  • Mobile usability: phone-style design, large buttons, touch scrolling.
  • Variable connectivity: local AI backup, manual mode, and demo data.
  • Source transparency: NASA POWER, Sentinel-2, ECOSTRESS, INTA, CIP.
  • Agronomic rigor: FAO-56, Kc, evapotranspiration, water balance, pH, texture, NPK.
  • Sustainability: emphasis on water efficiency and water recovery in the dome.
  • Education and accessibility: clear language, quick questions, and explanations.
  • Security and production: the Gemini API key is entered on the client side; for a real version, it should be managed on the backend.
  • Prototype limitations: it does not replace professional agronomic advice; some layers require internet, a Sentinel Hub instance ID, or API keys; results must be validated with field data.
